clue.text: Interested in time of abstinence, artist kept being illiberal

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: the fasting season kept the artist, so it holds those letters within itself

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter curious about a period of going without stayed narrow-minded all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' puts RA inside LENT, giving LERANT. RA, for a Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone illiberal is narrow-minded and unwilling to accept other views.

clue.text: Killer given gruesome representation in cinema

indicators.note: to represent something gruesomely is to show it in a mangled form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A murderer is portrayed in horrible detail on the big screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given gruesome representation' rearranges the letters of 'cinema'; the 'in' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang example: in American gangster talk a hired assassin is called this, since to ice is to murder.

clue.text: A number of times one gets nearly all the food

indicators.note: nearly all of a word is that word short of its last letter

parts.note: rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: On several occasions somebody ends up with almost everything on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' takes the E off 'the', leaving TH. The definition is vague on purpose: the number is three.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: three occasions is one particular count of occasions.

clue.text: Interesting ale? That may upset the guts to some extent!

indicators.note: to upset something is to overturn it, so the letters before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A curious beer could well give you a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That may upset' rearranges INTERESTING ALE. 'To some extent' is part of the definition: only a portion of the bowel is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the colon and its neighbours form one portion of the bowel.

clue.text: What makes for fatso — beer and Sunday dinner?

indicators.note: the answer is what can be made out of the letters that follow, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Booze and a big weekend lunch are how a person gets overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What makes for' rearranges FATSO and BEER together; the dash and 'and' only join. In Britain the traditional Sunday midday meal is a joint of meat with trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the classic British weekend family meal is this joint with Yorkshire pudding.

clue.text: Famous number associated with 50s rock-and-roller

parts.note: No is the written abbreviation of number
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes who followed rock and roll

explanation.surface: A well-known hit song is linked with a star from the early days of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted is a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth subculture with drape jackets and a taste for rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe somebody celebrated or well known.

clue.text: Little monster getting on in school

parts.note: ET is the small alien creature of Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: A naughty child is making good progress in class.
explanation.walkthrough: ET is the small alien of the Spielberg film; 'getting' and 'in' only join. The answer is a famous English boys' boarding college near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a famous English boarding college for boys.

clue.text: Like the guardian? Shame! 'Realy' badly misprinted!

parts.note: tut is the sound of mild disapproval

indicators.note: a badly misprinted word has its letters set in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A newspaper famous for typos has botched the spelling of a simple word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly misprinted' rearranges REALY into ELARY. The surface plays on The Guardian, a British newspaper nicknamed the Grauniad for its misprints.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the adjective describes something protective, serving as a protector.

clue.text: Refinements brought by pleasing neckwear

parts.note: nice means pleasing or agreeable
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Attractive cravats lend a man some polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are fine points or subtle details of polite behaviour.

clue.text: The rep proceeds awkwardly — no 'direct' language

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is clumsy and out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A salesman stumbles on with his pitch, never saying anything straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges THE REP PROCEEDS. In grammar the answer is the opposite of quoting someone's exact words.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: it is the indirect way of relaying what somebody said, without quoting.

clue.text: Sinful action admitted by terrorists

indicators.note: what a word admits it lets in, so the answer sits within the letters of that word

explanation.surface: Violent extremists confess to a wicked deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted by' shows the answer lies inside 'terrorists'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in religious language a moral lapse or wrongdoing is called this.

clue.text: Gold article given to national trust I initially considered genuine

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the is the definite article
NT abbreviates the National Trust, the British heritage charity

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A precious object donated to a heritage charity was at first thought by me to be the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the C of 'considered'. The National Trust is the charity that looks after Britain's historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean real, not a fake or copy.

clue.text: A new coin covering over one very old

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament

indicators.note: the coin covers over the next piece, so it wraps round it

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A freshly minted piece of money lies on top of an antique one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering over' puts I inside CENT, giving CIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe something dating from the distant past.

clue.text: Doctor before work allowed to get a little liquid

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A GP is permitted a small drink ahead of his shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tiny bead of water is a small amount of fluid.

clue.text: Hobby costing nothing? Also not bringing in extra money

parts.note: a hobby is an interest, something one pursues for pleasure
something free costs nothing

explanation.surface: A pastime that costs nothing also earns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half defines the answer as describing a loan on which the lender earns no additional charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a loan of this kind earns the lender no additional charge on top of the sum lent.

clue.text: Escape work in part

indicators.note: in places the short piece inside the longer word

parts.note: an element is a component part of something
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Getting away means doing the job only some of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' reads as 'partly', but 'in' is the insertion signal and 'part' is a word to be swapped for a synonym meaning component.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: lovers running away secretly to marry are making a getaway.

clue.text: Pose with 26 involved in incidents

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters before it are mixed together

parts.note: a cross-reference: the solution at 26 across supplies its four letters

explanation.surface: Someone striking an attitude gets caught up in various events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges POSE together with the four-letter answer to 26 across; 'with' and 'in' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are separate events or occurrences within a longer story.

clue.text: Engineers seen as vindicated

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
deemed means considered or regarded as

explanation.surface: Technical staff are regarded as having been proved right.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps. 'Seen as' looks like a link but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: someone cleared of blame has had their reputation restored.

clue.text: Poorly regarded woman's saleable item

definitions.meaning: an old disparaging expression for a woman, treating her as merchandise
literally one article out of a merchant's stock

explanation.definitionFit: Dated idiom: dictionaries give the phrase as a disparaging term for a female person, and literally it is an article of merchandise.

clue.text: Mean to call it a day after international

indicators.note: after says the stopping piece follows the other one

parts.note: to call it a day is to stop, to end

explanation.surface: A nasty decision to retire follows a match for one's country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean to' reads as 'plan to', but only 'Mean' defines and 'to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mean to do something is to plan or have it in mind.

clue.text: Scientist using different unit of weight

parts.note: something new is different from what went before
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A researcher adopts an unusual measure of heaviness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' only joins. The surface nods to the man himself, whose name was given to a unit of force.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Sir Isaac, the English physicist who described gravity.

clue.text: Person with loud voice occupying this tent originally

indicators.note: what occupies a place sits inside it, so the answer lies within the run of words after it

explanation.surface: A noisy camper was the first one living under this canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' shows the answer runs across 'this tent originally'. 'Originally' tempts you to take first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the Greek herald in the Iliad whose shout equalled fifty men gives his name to anyone booming.

clue.text: Re-establish Frenchman and wife

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man from Paris and his spouse are set up again.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to resume or restore something, such as a friendship, after a break.

clue.text: Area with river occupied by vessels

indicators.note: the river is occupied by the next piece, which therefore sits inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A stretch of land has a waterway full of boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by' is the insertion signal. The river is a Devon one in south-west England, and the vessels are the kitchen kind, not the boats the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are a wide stretch of land, sea or sky.

clue.text: I condemn a terrible authority

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters before it are disordered

explanation.surface: The speaker denounces a dreadful ruling power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges I CONDEMN A; in the surface it describes the power being denounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean control or power over others.

clue.text: Put up before court

parts.note: ere is the poetic word for before
Ct is the abbreviation of court in addresses

explanation.surface: Someone is brought to stand in front of a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up before' reads as one phrase, but 'before' is a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to raise or build a structure such as a tent.

clue.text: Team's affectation

definitions.meaning: a group of players on one part of a contest, such as eleven cricketers
British slang for swagger or pretentious airs, as in 'he puts on no airs'

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a sporting eleven, and British slang for pretentious airs or swagger.

clue.text: Society female (not nice) gets English chap emotionally aroused

parts.note: a witch is an unpleasant woman
Don is a man's name

explanation.surface: An unpleasant upper-class lady leaves a gentleman from England all excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' only joins. The bracketed aside belongs with 'female': together they give an unpleasant woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: both describe someone excited or stimulated.
